spacing.rule: Use 8 px inside a control group, 16 px between related groups, and 24 px between page sections. Increase by 8 px steps when hierarchy still reads as one group.

density.compactUse: Use small controls only inside dense toolbars, secondary filters, or expert tables with at least 12 visible rows.
density.largeUse: Use large controls for login, onboarding, or a single high-focus form.

surfaceHierarchy: The page canvas is level 0; a section surface or Card is level 1; Drawer and Modal are level 2.
Use one visual surface per topic. Keep related filter and result regions adjacent without adding decorative nested cards.
A page title belongs to the page header. Card titles name local sections.
stateLifecycle: initial: render the stable shell and a layout-matched skeleton when data is unavailable
loading: preserve context for refreshes and show bounded progress on the affected region
success: replace progress, announce completion, and refresh only the changed data
empty: distinguish first-use, no-data, and filtered-no-result states
error: keep entered values and the previous safe view; explain recovery and offer retry
permission: hide impossible navigation and explain disabled in-context actions
submitting: lock duplicate submission while keeping cancel behavior explicit
stale: show the last updated time and a refresh path when freshness affects decisions
content: Use concrete verb-object labels for actions, such as 新建版本, 导出记录, and 提交审核.
Use field labels as stable nouns. Place format examples and constraints in help text.
State messages contain current state, cause when known, and the next available action.
Keep technical IDs copyable and preserve their full value through ellipsis tooltips or a detail view.

cards.role: Persistent, in-context feedback that must remain visible while the user acts.
useWhen: A page or section has a blocking condition, degraded mode, policy notice, or recoverable error.
The message affects several controls and needs a stable reading position.
avoidWhen: Use Message for a brief confirmation after a completed action.
Use field validation for one invalid field.
Use Result for a full-page terminal state.
defaults: Place above the affected section and below the page header.
Use `showIcon`; write a one-line message and optional actionable description.
Reserve closable alerts for optional or already-understood notices.
states: info for neutral guidance
success for a completed page-level condition
warning for risk that still allows progress
error for blocked or failed work
composition: Keep at most one dominant alert per section.
Link or button actions must describe recovery, such as 重新加载 or 查看失败记录.
responsive: Allow the description and action to wrap; never reduce the icon or message below readable size.
a11y: Do not rely on tint alone; keep icon and explicit status copy.
Move focus only when the alert blocks the submitted task.
antiPatterns: Decorative success alerts on every normal page
Several stacked alerts with equal priority
Error text with no recovery path

cards.role: Compact count or presence signal attached to another label or object.
useWhen: A navigation item, tab, avatar, or icon needs a small unread count or dot status.
The count is secondary to the attached object.
avoidWhen: Use Tag for a row status that users must scan and compare.
Use Statistic for a primary metric.
Avoid a dot when the meaning is unavailable in text.
defaults: Cap large counts with `overflowCount`, usually 99.
Use status dots only for the fixed success, processing, warning, error, and default meanings.
states: zero hides when absence has no meaning
show zero when zero is a meaningful operational state
processing indicates ongoing work, not generic emphasis
composition: Attach the badge to one stable label or icon.
Keep the source label visible when the badge affects navigation.
responsive: Do not hide the parent label solely to save width; collapse the surrounding navigation with an accessible tooltip.
a11y: Expose the count and meaning in the accessible name.
Give dot badges a visible or screen-reader label.
antiPatterns: Using arbitrary colors for business status
Badge as a standalone table-cell status
Multiple badges on one label

cards.role: Trigger an immediate action or advance the current task.
useWhen: The user can execute a clear verb now.
The action changes state, opens a task surface, or submits data.
avoidWhen: Use a link for navigation to another content location.
Use Switch for an immediate binary setting.
Use Dropdown when more than two peer secondary actions compete for space.
defaults: Allow one primary button per task group and usually one in the first viewport.
Use medium size in back-office pages; keep a 8 px action gap.
Set `htmlType` explicitly inside Form.
Use `danger` only for destructive impact and pair irreversible actions with confirmation.
Loading preserves the button's label and stable outer width; delayed loading must not introduce a one-frame icon or gap jump.
states: loading locks duplicate submission, preserves the action label, and keeps layout stable
disabled includes an in-context explanation when permission or prerequisites block the action
success returns focus to the updated object or stable trigger
composition: Order low-risk actions before the primary action in page and form footers.
Expose at most two row actions; move the rest into Dropdown.
Icon-only buttons require a familiar symbol, Tooltip, and accessible name.
responsive: Keep the primary action visible; collapse secondary actions into Dropdown below 768 px.
Avoid full-width buttons in dense desktop toolbars; use full width for narrow form footers when it improves reachability.
a11y: Maintain a visible focus state and a 32 px minimum target, with 40 px preferred for touch.
Disabled controls do not receive hover events; wrap only when a Tooltip explanation is required.
antiPatterns: Several primary buttons in one group
Generic labels such as 确定 when the outcome can be named
Color-only custom button variants
Submitting again while loading

cards.role: Group one topic on a distinct surface when the boundary improves scanning.
useWhen: A dashboard module or detail section needs a stable topic boundary.
The module can move, load, or fail independently.
avoidWhen: Use spacing and a divider for closely related content.
Avoid wrapping every table, form, or metric solely to add a border.
Avoid Card inside Card.
defaults: Use 24 px internal rhythm on desktop and 16 px on compact layouts through tokens.
Card title names the local module; the page title stays outside.
Use `bordered` or a subtle surface distinction consistently across the page.
states: loading uses a layout-matched skeleton
empty keeps the same module height only when layout stability matters
error stays inside the card when the rest of the page remains usable
composition: Place actions in `extra` only when they affect the entire card.
Keep one primary reading order from title to summary to details to actions.
responsive: Cards stack to one column; internal grids reflow before horizontal scrolling.
a11y: Use a semantic heading level that follows the page outline.
Clickable cards need a single clear interactive target and keyboard behavior.
antiPatterns: Card nesting
Page title inside a content card
Equal visual weight for every page block
Whole-card click plus conflicting inner actions

cards.role: Provide one governed theme, locale, direction, component defaults, and popup policy to an application scope.
useWhen: The application needs shared AntD tokens, locale, component defaults, or popup behavior.
A product theme must remain consistent across pages and overlays.
avoidWhen: Avoid nesting providers for one-off visual exceptions.
Use component props or semantic styles for local variants.
Do not replace project business semantics with raw component-token overrides.
defaults: Keep one root provider and add scoped providers only for a documented product boundary.
Define brand values through tokens and component tokens before custom CSS.
Use the frozen semantic structure when styling internal parts.
states: theme and locale changes preserve readable content
popup containers remain inside the intended theme scope
provider updates avoid remounting page state
composition: Wrap the application shell so feedback APIs and overlays receive context.
Record every global token override in the project theme contract.
responsive: Use breakpoint-aware layout decisions in page composition; avoid switching provider themes by viewport.
a11y: Theme overrides maintain contrast and visible focus.
Locale and direction changes preserve control order and accessible names.
antiPatterns: Provider nested around individual controls
Structural `.ant-*` selectors used where semantic styles exist
Theme values duplicated in page CSS
Static feedback APIs outside provider context

cards.role: Select a date, time, or bounded range with calendar semantics.
useWhen: A date must be valid and comparable.
Users benefit from calendar context or a preset range.
avoidWhen: Use Input for partial dates or domain-specific codes.
Avoid time selection when the business only stores a date.
Avoid a range picker when start and end have different meanings or rules.
defaults: Use medium size and an explicit display format shared with table output.
Show common presets only when the product has stable meanings such as 今天, 近7天, and 本月.
Declare timezone and inclusive range behavior in help text when it affects results.
Model date and time constraints together; test range boundaries and avoid expensive work inside every disabled-cell callback.
states: allowClear restores the unset state when optional
invalid ranges explain the exact boundary
loading of disabled dates keeps the field stable
composition: Use RangePicker for one continuous interval.
Place quick ranges before advanced filters and preserve the selected range in the query summary.
responsive: Use a responsive popup container and allow the two range inputs to fit without truncating the date.
On narrow screens, open a full-width overlay or stack separate start/end fields when domain rules differ.
a11y: Keep labels explicit; placeholders do not replace labels.
Keyboard users must reach calendar cells, presets, and confirm actions in a stable order.
antiPatterns: Ambiguous 07/08 date formats
Hidden timezone conversion
Defaulting to a range that changes business results without explanation

cards.role: Read-only key-value facts for one object.
useWhen: A detail view contains stable labels and short values.
Users need to compare several facts about the same object.
avoidWhen: Use Table for several objects.
Use Form for editable fields.
Use prose or a code block for long unstructured content.
defaults: Use one column below 576 px, two columns from 768 px, and up to three columns at 1200 px when values remain readable.
Keep labels concise and visually quieter than values.
Use bordered style for dense administrative records; use unbordered grouped sections for narrative details.
states: missing optional values display —
unknown or failed values state the cause
copyable IDs remain full and selectable
composition: Group 6–12 related items per section.
Move long remarks, logs, and nested tables into their own section.
Place status and identity facts first.
responsive: Let long values span columns or occupy a dedicated row.
Never force labels into unreadable narrow columns.
a11y: Preserve label-value association through `items` semantics.
Links and copy actions include the value purpose in their accessible name.
antiPatterns: Using Descriptions as a layout grid
More than three columns of dense text
Hiding important facts behind collapsed panels by default

cards.role: Complete a contextual side task while preserving the underlying page.
useWhen: Editing or inspecting one row benefits from seeing the list context.
The task is longer than a quick decision and shorter than a full page.
The content follows a vertical reading flow.
avoidWhen: Use Modal for a short, focused decision.
Use a full page for multi-section tasks, broad tables, or work expected to exceed roughly five minutes.
Avoid nested drawers beyond one additional level.
defaults: Use 378 px for a short inspection, 520–600 px for a form, and 720 px for a complex record; choose a full page when 720 px still feels constrained.
Use `destroyOnHidden` when stale local state must be cleared.
Use `mask={{ closable: false }}` for dirty forms, destructive operations, or tasks that cannot tolerate accidental dismissal.
states: opening preserves the trigger and selected record
submitting disables duplicate close and submit paths
success closes only after persistence and returns focus to the trigger
cancel with dirty data asks whether to discard
composition: Header contains the object and task; body scrolls; footer actions stay visible.
Keep the primary action at the footer end and Cancel adjacent.
Use sections and dividers before adding inner cards.
responsive: Use width `100%` below 576 px and keep a visible close or back affordance.
Avoid fixed inner widths; form fields fill the available content column.
a11y: Set an explicit title and restore focus on close.
Keep keyboard focus within the drawer and announce async errors near the affected section.
antiPatterns: Deprecated `destroyOnClose` or `maskClosable` props
Table with many columns inside a narrow drawer
Dismissal that silently loses edits
Drawer used as permanent navigation

cards.role: Reveal secondary commands or choices from a compact trigger.
useWhen: Three or more secondary actions share the same object or scope.
A toolbar must preserve the primary action while compressing lower-priority commands.
avoidWhen: Keep the main action visible as a Button.
Use Select when choosing a form value.
Use context menus only when users can also reach the same commands visibly.
defaults: Use verb-object menu labels and stable ordering.
Separate destructive commands and style them as danger.
Use a text label plus chevron for ambiguous triggers; an ellipsis icon is acceptable in row actions.
states: disabled items explain prerequisites when the reason is actionable
loading belongs to the chosen command after the menu closes
selection updates the owning object and announces the result
composition: Limit the first level to roughly 7 items before grouping or moving to a dedicated surface.
Avoid submenus for frequently used operations.
responsive: Keep the popup inside the viewport and prefer vertical single-column menus.
a11y: Trigger exposes expanded state and menu purpose.
Keyboard navigation covers trigger, items, Escape, and focus restoration.
antiPatterns: Primary action hidden in the menu
Unlabeled ellipsis used outside an obvious row-action column
Mixing navigation, form values, and destructive commands without grouping

cards.role: Explain why expected content is absent and what the user can do next.
useWhen: A list, table, card, or page has no renderable business content after loading.
The absence has a distinct first-use, filtered, or permission meaning.
avoidWhen: Use Skeleton or Spin while loading.
Use Result for a terminal page outcome.
Avoid a decorative empty illustration when one concise line is enough.
defaults: First-use empty: explain value and offer the creation or import action.
Filtered empty: state that no results match and offer 清空筛选.
Data empty: state that no records exist without implying an error.
Permission empty: explain access and provide a request or return path.
states: keep filters and page context visible for filtered empty
do not show zero rows before the first request resolves
retry only when a request failed
composition: Use one short description and at most one primary recovery action.
Keep table column headers when they help users understand expected data.
responsive: Center within the available region without forcing an excessive minimum height.
a11y: Expose the empty reason as text.
Place focus on the recovery action only after an explicit failed submit or route transition.
antiPatterns: Same copy for all empty causes
No-results state that removes the filters
Empty shown during loading
Cheerful illustration for permission or error states

cards.role: Collect, validate, and submit a coherent set of user inputs.
useWhen: The task creates or edits an object.
Several fields share validation and one submission lifecycle.
avoidWhen: Use filters as a query form with explicit query/reset behavior.
Use Switch for an immediate standalone setting.
Use editable Table only when repeated row editing is the core task.
defaults: Use vertical layout for task forms, drawers, and modals; use horizontal layout for dense read-edit forms with short stable labels.
Keep the primary content column at 640–720 px; use two columns only for short, independent fields.
Group 4–8 related fields under a clear section heading.
Use medium controls and token spacing.
states: validate required and structural rules on blur or submit; validate dependent business rules after the dependency changes
preserve valid input after a failed submit
disable duplicate submit while `onFinish` is pending
reset only after confirmed success or explicit discard
composition: Order identity and prerequisites first, configuration second, optional remarks last.
Keep Cancel and Submit in a stable footer; name Submit by outcome.
Show field help before failure when the format is unfamiliar.
responsive: Collapse two-column fields to one column below 768 px.
Sticky footers must not cover the last field or validation message.
a11y: Every control has a persistent label.
Error messages identify the field and recovery.
On failed submit, focus the first invalid field and retain the error summary for complex forms.
antiPatterns: Placeholder used as the only label
More than two form columns
Clearing all values after a server error
Submit button separated from the end of the reading path

cards.role: Enter short free text or search text.
useWhen: The value cannot be selected from a stable finite set.
The user knows the identifier, name, or keyword to enter.
avoidWhen: Use InputNumber for quantitative values.
Use Select, Radio, or TreeSelect for known choices.
Use TextArea for content expected to exceed one line.
defaults: Use medium size and a width that reflects the expected value, usually 200–320 px in filters and full column width in forms.
Write format examples as help or a concrete placeholder, such as SN202607220001.
Use prefix/suffix only for stable units or recognizable affordances.
states: allow clear in filters and optional fields
preserve the entered value on validation and request errors
show character count only when a real limit exists
composition: Pair search input with an explicit query action when requests are costly.
Debounce live search and show request progress when results update asynchronously.
responsive: Allow filter inputs to fill their grid cell; avoid hard-coded widths wider than the viewport.
a11y: Label remains visible while typing.
Prefix and suffix icons have accessible names when interactive.
antiPatterns: Placeholder 请输入 with no format clue
Text input used for dates, booleans, or fixed statuses
Immediate request on every keystroke without debounce or progress

cards.role: Represent stable application information architecture and current location.
useWhen: A product has persistent sections and one selected route.
A collapsed or hierarchical navigation model is required.
avoidWhen: Use Tabs for peer views within one object or page.
Use Dropdown for commands.
Avoid deep hierarchy when a flatter information architecture can carry the product.
defaults: Keep labels short nouns and use one icon family.
Control `selectedKeys` from the route and `openKeys` from explicit user state.
Limit routine navigation to two visible levels; add a landing page before a third level.
states: selected reflects the current route
open reveals hierarchy without changing route
disabled navigation appears only when users benefit from seeing unavailable scope
composition: Group by user task and domain, not by database or team ownership.
Keep settings and account actions outside primary domain navigation.
responsive: Collapse the side navigation below the product breakpoint and retain labels through Tooltip or a temporary drawer.
Never expose a permanently horizontal-scrolling menu.
a11y: Current route is announced through selected state.
Keyboard users can traverse groups, submenus, and the collapse control.
antiPatterns: Menu used for row actions
More than two routine hierarchy levels
Selected state maintained separately from the route
Several unrelated icon styles

cards.role: Briefly confirm an action or report a transient global event.
useWhen: A completed action needs a short acknowledgement and the updated UI already shows the result.
A lightweight error can be retried from the unchanged context.
avoidWhen: Use Alert for persistent or actionable section feedback.
Use field validation for input errors.
Use Notification for longer background events that need title, details, or actions.
defaults: Use hook-based APIs through `App` or the relevant context holder so theme and locale apply.
Keep success copy to one outcome sentence.
Keep error messages visible long enough to read and repeat the recovery in the page when needed.
states: loading may transition in place to success or error for one async action
deduplicate repeated events with a stable key
close when the owning route is gone
composition: Do not stack more than three messages.
The page remains the durable source of truth after the toast disappears.
responsive: Allow long failure copy to wrap; move detailed diagnostics to an expandable or persistent surface.
a11y: Announce politely for success/info and assertively for a blocking error.
Avoid moving keyboard focus to a transient toast.
antiPatterns: Static API that misses ConfigProvider context
Toast as the only record of a failed operation
Technical exception text shown directly to users

cards.role: Focus attention on a short decision or compact task that blocks the current flow.
useWhen: A decision needs immediate resolution before continuing.
A compact form or preview can finish without broad page context.
The task is expected to take less than roughly one minute.
avoidWhen: Use Popconfirm for one simple row action.
Use Drawer when underlying context must remain visible.
Use a page for multi-section, large-table, or long-running work.
defaults: Use the 520 px default for confirmation and short forms; use 640–720 px for richer content; move wider tasks to Drawer or page.
Use `destroyOnHidden` when stale form state must be cleared.
Use `mask={{ closable: false }}` for destructive decisions and dirty forms.
Keep a specific title and concise consequence text.
states: confirm loading prevents duplicate submit and accidental close
validation stays in the modal
success closes after persistence and restores focus
failure keeps values and displays recovery
composition: Keep actions in the footer; Cancel precedes the outcome action.
Use neutral emphasis for decisions where the system must not steer the choice.
Avoid more than one scroll region and avoid nested modals.
responsive: Use responsive width with 16 px viewport margins below 576 px.
If the content requires persistent scrolling and a sticky footer, reevaluate Drawer or page.
a11y: Title labels the dialog.
Initial focus goes to the safest useful control; destructive confirmation does not pre-focus the destructive action.
Restore focus to the trigger.
antiPatterns: Deprecated `destroyOnClose` or `maskClosable` props
Modal used for a full CRUD page
Generic title 提示
Close that silently loses edits

cards.role: Keep a titled background-event result visible long enough to understand or act on it.
useWhen: A background task, cross-page event, or durable warning needs a title and supporting detail.
The user may need an action or enough time to read the result.
avoidWhen: Use Message for a short acknowledgement already reflected in the page.
Use Alert for feedback that belongs to a stable page section.
Use Modal only when progress must stop for a decision.
defaults: Use hook-based APIs through `App` or a context holder.
Use a stable key to update one event instead of adding duplicates.
Cap and stack notifications so the viewport remains readable; keep the newest outcome discoverable.
states: pending can update in place to success or failure
repeated events aggregate by stable key
actionable errors remain until dismissed or resolved
composition: Write a specific outcome title and one concise detail block.
Include at most one primary recovery action and one dismiss path.
Keep the page or task history as the durable record.
responsive: Keep 16 px viewport margins and a readable maximum width.
On narrow screens, avoid covering navigation and primary actions with a deep stack.
a11y: Announce urgency according to severity without moving focus.
Actions are keyboard reachable and retain context after dismissal.
antiPatterns: Static API that loses theme or locale
Unlimited notification pile
Same event repeated as separate cards
Critical recovery available only in a disappearing notification

cards.role: Navigate a bounded collection while preserving query context.
useWhen: The dataset cannot be shown or fetched as one manageable view.
Users need stable position, totals, or direct page access.
avoidWhen: Use virtual scrolling for continuous scanning where page position has no business meaning.
Hide pagination for a single page when the total is already visible.
defaults: Use page size 20 for standard tables, with 50 and 100 options for expert dense work.
Show the size changer when total exceeds 50.
Show total and current range for operational lists.
Use medium size with the table; use small only in compact secondary modules.
states: filter and sort normally return to page 1
preserve page only when remote behavior and user expectation are explicit
after deleting the last row on a page, move to the previous valid page
composition: Place at the table bottom end; place total/range at the opposite side when space allows.
Keep pagination state in the URL for shareable operational views.
responsive: Use simple mode or fewer visible page numbers below 576 px while preserving previous/next and current position.
a11y: Announce current page, total pages, and disabled previous/next states.
Page-size control has a visible or accessible label.
antiPatterns: Pagination with unknown meaning and no total
Resetting filters when page changes
Showing a size changer for tiny datasets
Infinite scroll for audit or selection-heavy tables

cards.role: Confirm one compact, local action close to its trigger.
useWhen: A row or item action has a clear short consequence.
The user needs a brief safety check without entering more information.
avoidWhen: Use Modal when consequences, policy, or input require more than two short sentences.
Skip confirmation for easy-to-undo low-risk actions and offer Undo instead.
Avoid for bulk operations with broad impact.
defaults: Name the object and consequence in the title.
Use an optional description for one key constraint.
Use `okButtonProps={{ danger: true }}` for destructive actions and name the confirm button by outcome.
states: async confirm shows loading and prevents repetition
failure keeps the popover or surfaces a persistent row error
success returns focus to a stable neighboring action when the row disappears
composition: Keep Cancel and the outcome action only.
Position within the viewport and away from table clipping containers.
responsive: Use Modal on narrow touch screens when the popover cannot remain readable or reachable.
a11y: Trigger, dialog text, and buttons are keyboard reachable.
Initial focus favors Cancel for irreversible operations.
antiPatterns: Generic 确定删除吗 without object context
Form fields inside Popconfirm
Confirmation added to every harmless action

cards.role: Choose one or several values from a known option set.
useWhen: The option set is known and usually contains 6–50 values.
The field needs search, clear, remote options, or compact form layout.
avoidWhen: Use Radio for 2–5 frequent mutually exclusive choices.
Use TreeSelect for hierarchical choices.
Use AutoComplete when free text remains valid.
Use Input when the option set is open-ended.
defaults: Use medium size and at least 160 px width; 200–240 px is the standard filter width.
Enable search for more than 10 options and define whether search is local or remote.
Use `allowClear` for optional filters and optional fields.
For multi-select, cap visible tags with responsive `maxTagCount` and preserve full selection access.
states: loading keeps the selected value and shows option progress
no options distinguishes unavailable source from no search match
remote errors offer retry
disabled explains permission or prerequisite when actionable
composition: Options use concise labels and stable values.
Group options only when groups help recognition.
Avoid custom option layouts that obscure keyboard selection.
responsive: Fill the grid cell on narrow layouts and keep popup width sufficient for the longest meaningful label.
a11y: Persistent label remains visible.
Search, active option, selected values, and clear action are announced.
antiPatterns: Hundreds of options loaded without search or virtualization
Multiple selection used as a substitute for a filter builder
Placeholder used as label
Option labels that expose internal enum keys

cards.role: Preserve layout and communicate first-load structure before content is available.
useWhen: Initial data is expected to take longer than roughly 300 ms.
The final layout is predictable and visual stability matters.
avoidWhen: Use Spin for a small refresh while existing content remains useful.
Use Progress when real completion can be measured.
Avoid skeletons for instant local transitions.
defaults: Match the count, shape, and hierarchy of the final modules.
Delay briefly to prevent flash on fast responses.
Use active animation only while work is progressing.
states: initial shell plus skeleton
success swaps the region without large layout shift
error replaces skeleton with a clear recovery state
timeout stops the illusion of progress and exposes status
composition: Use table-row skeletons for table first load and card skeletons for dashboard modules.
Keep stable page header and navigation visible.
responsive: Match the responsive layout that will replace it; do not keep desktop columns on a narrow viewport.
a11y: Mark the region busy and provide a concise loading label.
Skeleton shapes remain hidden from the accessibility tree.
antiPatterns: Generic paragraph skeleton for every page
Skeleton shown over existing useful data during refresh
Indefinite skeleton after request failure

cards.role: Indicate bounded asynchronous work inside an existing region.
useWhen: Refreshing a table, card, form dependency, or action region while layout remains stable.
The result duration is unknown and no numeric progress exists.
avoidWhen: Use Skeleton for page first load.
Use Progress for upload, import, or processing with measurable completion.
Avoid blocking the whole page for one local request.
defaults: Delay the indicator for fast work.
Keep prior content visible with reduced interaction when it remains trustworthy.
Add a short tip for waits that exceed routine feedback.
states: busy marks the smallest affected region
success removes progress and updates content
error ends progress and exposes retry
cancellation restores the last safe state
composition: Pair button loading with the triggering action; use Spin for the content region.
Avoid several simultaneous spinners without a clear owning scope.
responsive: Center within the affected container, not the viewport, unless the entire route is loading.
a11y: Set `aria-busy` and announce the loading purpose.
Do not trap focus in a non-modal loading region.
antiPatterns: Full-screen spinner for a row request
Spinner that survives a failed request
Loading text with no owned region

cards.role: Show progress through an ordered task with meaningful stages.
useWhen: A task has 3–7 dependent stages and users need orientation or resumability.
Each stage has its own validation or completion state.
avoidWhen: Use Tabs for peer views with no required order.
Use Timeline for historical events.
Avoid Steps for a short form that fits one page.
defaults: Use short noun or verb-object titles and optional concise descriptions.
Keep current, completed, waiting, and error states derived from workflow truth.
Persist completed data before advancing when recovery matters.
states: current step owns validation
error marks the affected step and keeps values
completed steps can be reviewed when policy allows
submitting the final step has a distinct processing state
composition: Place step content below the indicator with one clear title.
Footer order stays Previous, Save draft when relevant, Next or Submit.
Summarize irreversible choices before final submission.
responsive: Use vertical or compact label placement below 768 px.
Keep long descriptions in the content area instead of the step label.
a11y: Announce current step and total count.
Changing steps updates the page heading and focus.
antiPatterns: Clickable future steps that bypass validation
Steps used as decorative status dots
More than seven stages with full labels
No recovery after a failed step

cards.role: Immediately toggle one binary setting.
useWhen: The change takes effect immediately and the two states are unambiguous.
The setting can safely show a pending state.
avoidWhen: Use Checkbox when the value is submitted with a form.
Use Radio when users need to compare labeled alternatives.
Avoid Switch for destructive or multi-consequence changes without confirmation.
defaults: Use a stable noun label and explain both states in nearby copy when the effect is unfamiliar.
Use loading while persistence is pending.
Revert to the last confirmed state on failure and explain recovery.
states: checked and unchecked map to explicit business values
loading blocks repeat toggles
disabled explains policy when useful
composition: Place the label before the switch in forms and settings rows.
Confirmation appears before committing high-impact toggles.
responsive: Keep label and switch on the same row when readable; wrap help text below.
a11y: Accessible name describes the setting, and checked state communicates the value.
Color is supplemented by position and label.
antiPatterns: Save button required after an apparently immediate switch
On/off meaning hidden in a vague label
Optimistic state left incorrect after request failure

cards.role: Scan, compare, sort, filter, select, and operate on structured records.
useWhen: Rows share a stable schema and users compare values across columns.
Sorting, filtering, pagination, selection, or row operations are core tasks.
avoidWhen: Use List or cards for heterogeneous narrative objects.
Use Descriptions for one record.
Use a data-grid product only when cell editing, spreadsheet navigation, or very large virtualization is the primary workflow.
defaults: Use `size=medium` for standard back-office pages; use small for expert dense views with at least 12 visible rows.
Keep the first meaningful identity column visible and allow it to flex from 160 px.
Use widths: selection 48, index 64, status 96–120, short ID 120–160, date/time 160–184, numeric 96–120 right-aligned, action 120–200.
Expose at most two row actions; move additional actions into Dropdown.
Use horizontal scroll with `x=max-content` when required and fix only identity and action columns when the viewport still preserves useful data.
At both scroll edges, header, body, sticky bar, and fixed-column boundaries must stay aligned within one CSS pixel at tested zoom levels.
states: first load uses row-matched skeleton
refresh preserves rows and selection only when keys remain valid
filtered empty keeps filters and headers
request error preserves the last safe rows with a stale indicator
bulk selection clears after a completed destructive mutation
composition: Place a query form above, page and batch actions in a toolbar, the table next, and pagination at the bottom.
Keep 3–4 high-frequency filters visible at 1200 px and collapse the rest under 更多筛选.
Summaries belong above or below the table based on whether they guide filtering or reconcile results.
Render status through one project-level semantic mapping.
responsive: Assign column priority and hide low-priority columns by breakpoint before forcing scroll.
At narrow widths, keep identity, status, and one action; offer a detail view for the rest.
Never shrink text until identifiers, dates, or actions become ambiguous.
a11y: Provide stable `rowKey`, row headers where appropriate, sortable labels, and selection names.
Keyboard and screen-reader users receive selected count, sort direction, and update announcements.
antiPatterns: All columns auto-sized with no priority
Centered numbers or dates
Five or more visible row actions
Color-only statuses
Pagination and filter state disconnected
Fixed columns covering overlays

cards.role: Switch between peer views of the same object or task scope.
useWhen: Two to seven views share one page identity and users switch frequently.
Each tab can load and fail independently without changing the main object.
avoidWhen: Use Menu for product navigation.
Use Steps for ordered progress.
Use segmented controls for a small display mode that changes the same data view.
defaults: Use concise parallel labels and keep the default tab aligned to the primary user goal.
Persist the active key in the URL when direct links and back navigation matter.
Use counts only when they aid prioritization and remain fresh.
states: lazy load heavy panels
preserve safe panel state when switching
show errors inside the owning panel
remove or disable inaccessible tabs according to whether awareness helps the user
composition: Place tabs below the page or object header.
Keep page-wide actions outside; tab-specific actions live inside the panel.
Avoid a second tab row unless the hierarchy is explicit and rare.
responsive: Allow tab-bar overflow scrolling with clear edge affordances; avoid truncating every label.
Consider Dropdown only for low-frequency overflow tabs.
a11y: Use proper tab/tabpanel association and keyboard arrow navigation.
Focus remains predictable when panels load asynchronously.
antiPatterns: Tabs used as primary application navigation
Tabs mixed with workflow steps
All panels mounted with expensive requests
Page actions changing as an unexplained side effect of tab switch

cards.role: Show a compact category, state, property, or removable selection.
useWhen: A short label must be scanned inside a table, description, or filter summary.
A category or lifecycle state benefits from shape plus text.
avoidWhen: Use Badge for an attached count or dot.
Use Button for actions.
Use plain text for low-priority metadata that does not need a chip shape.
defaults: Use `variant=filled` for standard semantic status, `solid` for rare high-emphasis states, and `outlined` for neutral categories.
Use functional colors for success, warning, error, and processing; use preset colors for stable categories.
Keep one status-to-visual mapping across the project.
states: loading and unknown receive explicit labels
closable tags remove a user-selected value
checkable tags behave as controls and expose selection
composition: Keep text to roughly 2–8 Chinese characters.
Show at most three tags in a table cell; summarize overflow with +N and full access.
responsive: Wrap category groups deliberately; keep primary row height stable in dense tables.
a11y: Text carries the meaning; color supplements it.
Interactive tags have control semantics and keyboard focus.
antiPatterns: Deprecated `bordered` prop
Random colors per page
Every metadata value rendered as a tag
Tag styled to look like a button

cards.role: Reveal concise supplementary meaning for a compact visible target.
useWhen: An icon-only control needs a name.
Truncated content needs its full value.
A disabled action needs a short reason and another visible path explains resolution.
avoidWhen: Keep essential instructions, errors, and policy visible.
Avoid tooltips for long content, forms, or touch-only discovery.
Do not attach to every familiar labeled control.
defaults: Keep content to one or two short lines.
Use a small open delay for dense table icons and avoid flicker between adjacent targets.
Wrap disabled controls only when event delivery requires it.
states: open follows hover and focus
close on Escape and when the target disappears
updated content remains stable while open
composition: Name icon actions with a verb.
For truncated IDs, include a separate copy action when copying is common.
responsive: Ensure popup placement, arrow, and target alignment stay inside the viewport at every edge; provide a visible alternative on touch.
a11y: Tooltip content associates with the target and appears on keyboard focus.
Target already has an accessible name; Tooltip adds visible support.
antiPatterns: Required field rule available only on hover
Tooltip containing several paragraphs or buttons
Tooltip used to hide ambiguous icon design

cards.role: Browse, inspect, and select items whose hierarchy is central to understanding the data.
useWhen: Users need to explore or operate on a visible hierarchy.
Expanded ancestry and sibling context affect the decision.
avoidWhen: Use TreeSelect when hierarchy is only an input field.
Use a flat Table or List when nesting adds no decision value.
Avoid rendering a large remote hierarchy without lazy loading and search.
defaults: Define checked conduction for parent, child, disabled, and partially checked nodes before implementation.
Use `checkStrictly` when the product requires independent selection.
Preserve expanded and selected state by stable keys.
states: loading is local to the expanding node
disabled nodes retain an explicit meaning
half-checked state reflects the chosen conduction rule
remote failure preserves visible ancestors
composition: Place search above large trees and keep the matched path visible.
For permission changes, summarize the effective scope before submission.
responsive: Use a Drawer or full-width surface on narrow screens so labels and depth remain readable.
a11y: Expose level, expanded, selected, checked, half-checked, and disabled state.
Keyboard navigation supports parent, child, sibling, expand, and selection movement.
antiPatterns: Default cascade accepted without product decision
Disabled-node behavior left ambiguous
Deep tree without search
Color-only checked or disabled meaning

cards.role: Choose values from a hierarchy while preserving parent-child context.
useWhen: Departments, locations, categories, or permissions have meaningful hierarchy.
Users need search plus tree context in one field.
avoidWhen: Use Select for a flat option set.
Use Tree when browsing or managing hierarchy is the main task.
Avoid for more than a few thousand remote nodes without lazy loading and search strategy.
defaults: Use medium size and a 240–320 px field in filters.
Choose parent, child, disabled-node, and half-checked behavior explicitly; do not rely on default cascade semantics.
Enable search and define whether results preserve ancestors.
Use responsive tag limits for multiple selection.
states: lazy nodes show local loading
selected paths remain readable
missing permissions explain why a branch is unavailable
remote failure preserves prior selections
composition: Labels use domain names; add full path only when duplicate labels exist.
For high-risk permission trees, add a review summary before submission.
responsive: Use a wide popup or full-width mobile surface so hierarchy labels remain readable.
a11y: Expose expanded, selected, checked, and level state.
Keyboard navigation covers tree movement and search results.
antiPatterns: Flat choices forced into a tree
Unclear parent selection cascade
Thousands of nodes rendered at once
Selected tag overflow hiding the scope of a permission change

cards.role: Express page hierarchy, readable content, identifiers, and constrained text with the AntD type system.
useWhen: Text needs AntD hierarchy, copyability, editability, or ellipsis behavior.
A page needs consistent titles, secondary text, code values, and paragraphs.
avoidWhen: Avoid using heading styles only to change font size.
Keep data tables on their native cell semantics.
Do not hide critical instructions behind ellipsis.
defaults: Follow the page heading outline and the 14/22 base text rhythm.
Use subdued text for metadata while preserving readable contrast.
For multiline ellipsis, test actual fonts, width changes, mixed scripts, and expandable recovery.
states: copy and edit actions provide progress and outcome
truncated content offers full access
loading text reserves stable space
composition: Pair one page title with concise context and keep section headings parallel.
Use code styling for identifiers only when it aids scanning or copying.
responsive: Allow text to wrap before reducing font size.
Recalculate ellipsis after container and font changes without layout oscillation.
a11y: Heading levels follow document structure.
Truncated text remains available to keyboard and assistive technology users.
antiPatterns: Heading level chosen by appearance
Low-contrast secondary text
Ellipsis with no full-value access
Several unrelated font scales on one page

cards.role: Select files and manage validation, transfer, processing, retry, and removal as one lifecycle.
useWhen: A task requires local files, images, documents, firmware, or import data.
Users need visible per-file state and recovery.
avoidWhen: Use an import workflow when upload is only the first stage of parsing, mapping, validation, and commit.
Avoid drag-and-drop when exact file selection is safer or space is limited.
Avoid hiding security and format constraints until failure.
defaults: Declare accepted types, maximum size, maximum count, and naming rules next to the trigger.
Controlled `fileList` always includes `onChange` and a stable UID strategy.
Validate client-side with `beforeUpload`; repeat authoritative validation on the server.
Show file name, size when relevant, progress, outcome, retry, and remove.
states: selected
validating
uploading with progress
uploaded
server-processing
success
failed with reason and retry
removed or cancelled
composition: Use `maxCount=1` for replacement assets.
For batch import, hand off successful uploads to a separate preview/validation/commit stage.
Dangerous file replacement names the target and keeps version history when possible.
responsive: File rows wrap metadata and keep retry/remove actions reachable.
Drop zones become compact selectors on narrow screens when drag precision is poor.
a11y: Trigger names accepted content.
Progress and per-file result are announced.
Keyboard users can select, retry, preview, and remove files.
antiPatterns: Controlled `fileList` without `onChange`
Success shown before server processing finishes
Only file extension checked
Failure that clears the file and reason
Real upload triggered in a demo-only project

cards.role: Switch a small display mode or filter of the same content in place.
useWhen: Two to five mutually exclusive options change how one region is viewed or filtered, such as 全部 / 告警 / 离线 or 列表 / 卡片.
The associated region updates in place without changing page identity or route.
avoidWhen: Use Tabs when each option owns a peer content panel or section with its own actions and loading state.
Use Radio for a form field that is submitted with the form.
Use Select when there are many options or the labels are long.
Use Menu for product navigation.
defaults: Keep exactly one option selected; the first option is the default unless a stored preference exists.
Use short parallel labels; add an icon only with a text label or an accessible name.
Use the controlled value and onChange when the choice is synced to the URL or a table query.
Use the medium size, and block width when the control sits alone in a narrow toolbar.
states: selected option is visually distinct without relying on color alone
disabled option explains why in nearby help text
the controlled region shows its own loading state while switching
keep filters and scroll position when the switch does not change the data scope
composition: Place it directly above or beside the region it controls, usually in the toolbar next to filters.
Keep page-wide actions outside the control and do not mix action buttons into the options.
responsive: Use block width on narrow screens; switch to Select when the labels no longer fit on one line.
Use vertical orientation only in a narrow side region.
a11y: The options behave as a radio group; keep arrow-key navigation and a visible focus ring.
Give icon-only options an accessible name, and set name when several groups share one page.
antiPatterns: Segmented used as page navigation
More than five options or long labels forced into one row
Segmented used for a value submitted with a form
Segmented switching unrelated content sections that need Tabs
No option selected

cards.role: Report the outcome of an important operation or a whole page and offer the next action.
useWhen: An important operation or route has finished and the feedback is complex: success, failure, warning, 403, 404, or 500.
The whole page or flow step has nothing else to show except the outcome and what to do next.
avoidWhen: Use Empty when a list, table, or card region simply has no data.
Use Message or Notification for transient feedback that does not replace the page.
Use Alert for an inline banner while the surrounding content stays usable.
Use Skeleton or Spin while loading.
defaults: Set status to match the outcome: success, error, info, warning, 403, 404, or 500.
Title states the outcome; subTitle states the cause when known and the next step.
Put at most one primary and one secondary action in extra, such as 返回列表 and 重试.
Permission 403: explain the access rule and offer a request or return path.
states: show only after the request or route has settled, never during loading
on failure keep entered values reachable through the retry path
on success offer the follow-up action and a way to continue
composition: Center it in the page content area under the application shell.
Use a custom icon only when the built-in status icon does not convey the outcome.
responsive: Keep icon, title, subTitle, and extra stacked and centered; let actions wrap under narrow width.
a11y: Expose the outcome as text; do not rely on the status icon alone.
Move focus to the title or the primary action after a submit result or route transition.
antiPatterns: Result used for an empty table or filtered-no-result state
Success result without a next action
Generic 出错了 copy with no cause or recovery
Result used for transient confirmation that a Message would cover
Result nested inside a card that still shows other content
